cuerpo: Gilgamesh, two-thirds god and one-third man, rules Uruk with perfect strength but boundless arrogance. The nobles complain to the gods, for the king leaves no son to his father and no maiden to her mother, abusing his power day and night.
prompt: Una panorámica de la imponente ciudad de Uruk con sus murallas de ladrillo cocido; en lo alto de un zigurat, un rey de porte divino observa con desdén a su pueblo exhausto.
alt: Sculpted relief: a panorama of walled Uruk beneath a radiant sun; from the ziggurat, the king watches over his people.
cita: Gilgamesh leaves no son to his father, no maiden to the warrior, no wife to her husband.

cuerpo: Heeding the complaints, the goddess Aruru fashions Enkidu from clay, a wild being meant to be Gilgamesh’s rival. Enkidu lives on the steppe, his body covered in hair; he lives at peace among the beasts and protects them from hunters.
prompt: En un paisaje natural primigenio, la diosa Aruru moldea una figura humana gigantesca y velluda a partir de barro rojizo, rodeada de animales salvajes.
alt: Sculpted relief: a figure clad in skins reaches out among wild animals in a primeval landscape.
cita: Aruru washed her hands, pinched off a little clay and cast it on the ground: so she created Enkidu.

cuerpo: To civilise Enkidu, Gilgamesh sends a hierodule, a sacred prostitute. After six days and seven nights of human love, Enkidu finds that the animals flee from him; his bodily strength wanes, but his mind grows “wise” and he comes to understand the world.
prompt: En un oasis mesopotámico, Enkidu se sienta junto a una mujer vestida con finas telas, mirando con tristeza cómo una manada de gacelas escapa hacia el horizonte.
alt: Sculpted relief: Enkidu seated beside a woman in a palm oasis while a herd moves away in the background.
cita: You are sublime, Enkidu; you shall be like a god.

titulo: The Meeting and the Heroic Friendship
cuerpo: Enkidu arrives in Uruk to challenge the king’s tyranny. The two fight fiercely before the House of the Assembly “like two wild bulls”, but once they recognise each other as equals the struggle ends, and they seal an unbreakable friendship that will bind them for ever.
prompt: Dos guerreros de proporciones heroicas y vestimentas reales luchando en una plaza pública rodeada de muros de adobe; la escena muestra el momento en que la violencia se transforma en un abrazo.
alt: Relief carved in pale stone: two Mesopotamian warriors locked in combat, surrounded by figures and scrolls.
cita: Gilgamesh set his foot upon the ground: his anger abated, his breast grew calm.

titulo: The Expedition to the Cedar Forest
cuerpo: Seeking eternal glory and to “win a name”, Gilgamesh resolves to travel to the Cedar Forest and defeat Humbaba, the monstrous guardian appointed by the gods. Despite Enkidu’s fear, Gilgamesh insists that only the gods are immortal and that a man must fight for his fame.
prompt: Los dos héroes, armados con hachas y puñales de oro, de pie ante la entrada de un bosque de cedros milenarios cuyas cumbres tocan las nubes.
alt: Sculpted relief: two armed figures before the entrance to a forest of immense trees closing into shadow.
cita: If I fall, I shall have established my name.

cuerpo: Helped by the eight winds sent by the god Shamash, the heroes pin Humbaba down. Though the giant begs for mercy, the friends kill him and cut off his head, destroying the guardian of the sacred forest.
prompt: Una escena de batalla épica bajo un cielo de tormenta; ráfagas de viento golpean a un gigante monstruoso mientras los héroes asestan el golpe final.
alt: Sculpted relief: a horned monstrous creature lashed by the wind beneath a sky torn with red.
cita: His roar is a flood, his mouth is fire, his breath is death.

titulo: The Rejection of Ishtar and the Bull of Heaven
cuerpo: The goddess Ishtar falls in love with Gilgamesh, but he rejects her with insults, reminding her of the fate of her former lovers. Enraged, Ishtar sends the Bull of Heaven to destroy Uruk, but the two friends kill it and humiliate the goddess.
prompt: El enorme cadáver de un toro alado en las calles de Uruk; Gilgamesh desafía a Ishtar, quien observa con rabia desde las almenas de la muralla.
alt: Sculpted relief: the carcass of the Bull of Heaven felled before a winged figure, with the city behind.
cita: Enkidu attacked the Bull of Heaven and seized it by its thick tail.

cuerpo: The gods decide that Enkidu must die as punishment for the friends’ deeds. Enkidu falls ill and has terrifying visions of the world of the dead. After his death, Gilgamesh sinks into utter grief, mourning his friend like a hired mourner and refusing to accept his loss.
prompt: Un rey con la túnica rasgada y ceniza en la cabeza, llorando desconsoladamente sobre el cuerpo sin vida de su compañero en una habitación real sombría.
alt: Sculpted relief: a figure covers his face with his hands, bent over a body laid out and wrapped in cloth.
cita: Gilgamesh wept bitterly for his friend, and lay stretched upon the ground.

titulo: The Journey through the Mountains of Mashu
cuerpo: Terrified of his own death, Gilgamesh sets out to find Ut-napishtim and gain eternal life. On his way he must cross the mountains of Mashu, where he meets the fearsome scorpion-men, guardians of the gates of the Sun.
prompt: Un viajero exhausto cubierto con pieles de fieras frente a dos colosales figuras híbridas con torsos humanos y colas de escorpión gigantescas.
alt: Sculpted relief: a traveller in animal skins advances between two colossal scorpion guardians with raised tails.
cita: Scorpion-men guard its gate: their terror is so deep that to look on them is death.

titulo: The Meeting with Ut-napishtim and the Flood
cuerpo: Gilgamesh crosses the “Waters of Death” and finds Ut-napishtim, who reveals that immortality was a unique gift granted after he survived the Great Flood, and explains that the gods decide life and death without revealing the final day.
prompt: Un anciano sabio de túnica blanca sentado en una isla remota, relatando una historia mientras al fondo se vislumbra el arca encallada en la cima de una montaña.
cita: I looked about in every direction, and behold: all was sea.
alt: Relief: an old sage in a white robe seated beneath an ancient tree; behind him, the ark aground on the mountaintop after the Flood.

titulo: The Plant of Youth and the Final Failure
cuerpo: Ut-napishtim reveals where to find a plant that restores youth. Gilgamesh brings it up from the bottom of the sea, but while he bathes, a serpent steals it. The hero finally understands that his only lasting legacy will be the walls of Uruk that he himself built.
prompt: Un hombre de rodillas llorando junto a un manantial, mientras una serpiente se desliza entre las rocas con una planta resplandeciente; al fondo brillan las murallas de la ciudad.
alt: Sculpted relief: a man weeps on his knees beside a spring while a serpent carries off the plant; behind him, the walls.
cita: A serpent rose swiftly; the plant slipped from his hands.

titulo: What Remains: the Walls of Uruk
cuerpo: Back in Uruk, without the plant and without his friend, Gilgamesh climbs with Urshanabi the ferryman to the top of the walls he had built. He asks him to examine the foundations, the baked brick, the seven layers of bitumen: the work still stands. He did not win eternal life, but he discovers another kind of permanence: the kind a well-built city leaves behind. The king who began by abusing his strength ends by understanding what power is truly for.
prompt: Gilgamesh y el barquero Urshanabi de pie en la cima de las murallas de Uruk al amanecer, contemplando la ciudad de ladrillo cocido bajo un cielo que se abre.
cita: Examine its foundation, inspect its brickwork: see if its wall is not of baked brick.
alt: Mesopotamian relief: a winged, curly-bearded figure emerges from the stone, and to his right a cleft of light cuts through the rock toward what opens beyond.
